hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT DISTINCT a.seat_id
FROM Cinema a
JOIN Cinema b ON ABS(a.seat_id - b.seat_id) = 1
WHERE a.free = 1 AND b.free = 1
ORDER BY a.seat_id ASC;
```

variables: N: number of records in Cinema table
complexity.notes: Equi-join on adjacent seat distance and sorting distinct seats executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all combinations without adjacency predicates creates full quadratic row scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Self-join on absolute difference 1 avoids complex multi-row grouping.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of ABS difference or LEAD/LAG window functions to check neighboring seats.

solutions.approach: Self Join on Adjacent Seat Identifiers

solutions.code:
SELECT DISTINCT a.seat_id
FROM Cinema a
JOIN Cinema b ON ABS(a.seat_id - b.seat_id) = 1
WHERE a.free = 1 AND b.free = 1
ORDER BY a.seat_id ASC;

import pandas as pd

def consecutive_available_seats(cinema: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = cinema.sort_values(by='seat_id')
    free = df['free'] == 1
    prev_free = free.shift(1, fill_value=False)
    next_free = free.shift(-1, fill_value=False)
    res = df[free & (prev_free | next_free)]
    return res[['seat_id']]
